r0.why: Definition via four operations like rationals [1]; fundamental, used in algebra and number theory [2]; Q, R, C best known [3].

r1.why: Set with two binary operations [18], binary operation definition [19], axioms: associativity, commutativity, identities 0 and 1 distinct, inverses, distributivity [22]-[28].

r2.why: Inverses allow subtraction and division as defined [15][16]; division by zero excluded [32]; rational fractions and their inverses [38][39].

r3.why: Product formula and closure so C is a field [40][41]; point or arrow with length and angle [42]; parallelogram addition, angles add and lengths multiply (rotate and scale) [43].

r4.why: Scalars for vector spaces [10]; analysis on fields with extra structure and real-number properties [8][9]; number and function fields [11][12]; finite fields in codes and cryptography [13]; R and C in sciences [44].

r5.why: Ancient compass-straightedge problems [45]; field theory in trisection and squaring-the-circle proofs [5]; Galois theory and Abel-Ruffini [6].
